From today's featured article
[31]<a title=Mark Satin />
[32]<a >Mark Satin />
(born November
16, 1946) is an American
[33]<a title=List of political th...>political theorist />
and writer. He contributed to the development of
[34]<a title=Nonviolence>neopacifism />
in the 1960s,
[35]<a title=New Age>New Age politics />
in the 1970s and 1980s, and
[36]<a >radical centrism />
from the 1990s into the 2020s. After emigrating to Canada to avoid serving in the
[37]<a >Vietnam War />
, he wrote the
Manual for Draft-Age Immigrants to Canada
, which sold nearly 100,000 copies. Then came
New Age Politics
(1978), which identifies an emergent third force pursuing such goals as
[38]<a >simple living />
,
[39]<a title=Decentralization>decentralism />
, and
[40]<a title=Global citizenship>global responsibility />
. Satin spread his ideas by co-founding the
[41]<a >New World Alliance />
and publishing the newsletter
New Options
. He also co-drafted "Ten Key Values", the foundational statement of the
[42]<a >Green Party of the United States />
. Following a period of political disillusion, Satin wrote
Radical Middle
(2004), which criticizes political partisanship and promotes mutual learning and innovative policy syntheses. In 2023, Satin wrote
Up From Socialism: My 60-Year Search for a Healing New Radical Politics
.
(
*[43]<a title=Mark Satin>Full
article... />
)

Help us improve this article!
[70]<a title=Garbage bin with tra... />
Garbage bin with trash on top
This week's article for improvement is
[71]<a >garbage />
, waste material discarded by humans. The words
garbage
,
refuse
,
rubbish
, and
trash
are generally used interchangeably.
You can improve this article by:
Expanding the "Treatment", "Disposal", and "History" sections
Finding
[72]<a title=Wikipedia:Reliable s...>reliable sources />
about garbage disposal
Using
[73]<a title=Talk:Garbage>sources mentioned on the talk page />
to add content to the article
You can
[74]<a title=Wikipedia:Be bold>be bold />
and
[75]<a >start editing the article />
. Have questions or suggestions? Visit
[76]<a title=Talk:Garbage>the article's talk page />
, or post at the
[77]<a title=Wikipedia:Teahouse>Teahouse />
for general discussion.

From today's featured list
*[148]<a title=Mohamed Muizzu />
Mohamed Muizzu
*[149]<a title=List of presidents o...>There have been eight presidents of the Maldives />
since 1953. The
*[150]<a >president of the Maldives />
is the country's
*[151]<a >head of state />
and
*[152]<a >head of government />
, and is
*[153]<a title=Direct election>directly elected />
by the citizens of the country through a popular vote for a five-year term. The president serves as the
*[154]<a >commander-in-chief />
of the
*[155]<a >Maldives National Defence Force />
and leads the
*[156]<a >cabinet of the Maldives />
. Since 1968, two presidents (
*[157]<a >Ibrahim Nasir />
and
*[158]<a >Mohamed Nasheed />
) have resigned from the post.
*[159]<a >Mohamed Amin Didi />
was the shortest-serving president, serving for 7 months and 21 days in 1953.
*[160]<a >Maumoon Abdul Gayoom />
served as president for 30 years, from 1978 to 2008, making him the longest-serving president of the Maldives and one of the longest-serving presidents in Asia. The incumbent president is
*[161]<a >Mohamed Muizzu />
(pictured)
, who assumed office on 17
November 2023. (
*[162]<a title=List of presidents o...>Full
list... />
)

Today's featured picture
*[168]<a title=Space Shuttle Atlant... />
*[169]<a title=Space Shuttle Atlant...>Space Shuttle
Atlantis />
was a NASA
*[170]<a >Space Shuttle orbiter />
that flew 33 missions between 1985 and 2011 as part of the United States'
*[171]<a >Space Shuttle program />
. Built by
*[172]<a >Rockwell International />
,
Atlantis
made its maiden flight on 3
October 1985 and was subsequently used to deploy the spacecraft
*[173]<a title=Magellan (spacecraft...>Magellan />
to Venus and
*[174]<a title=Galileo (spacecraft)>Galileo />
to Jupiter. It conducted seven missions to the Russian space station
*[175]<a >Mir />
, helped assemble the
*[176]<a >International Space Station />
(ISS), and carried out the final servicing mission to the
*[177]<a >Hubble Space Telescope />
. In July 2011,
Atlantis
completed
*[178]<a >STS-135 />
, the Space Shuttle program's final mission. It is now exhibited at the
*[179]<a >Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex />
in Florida. This photograph of
Atlantis
was taken in May
2010 from the ISS, shortly after it undocked during
*[180]<a >STS-132 />
.
Photograph credit:
*[181]<a >NASA />
